description: Verify that DUT TCP treats the receive window as an unsigned 16-bit number — an MSB-set advertised window does not refuse the send (RFC 1122 §4.2.2.3 p83)
approach:
[Objective]
The Window field is unsigned 16-bit. A naive parser using signed arithmetic would treat the MSB-set value as negative and refuse to send. RFC 1122 §4.2.2.3 / RFC 793 §3.1 mandate unsigned interpretation.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester ⇄ DUT: handshake; tester advertises a Window value with MSB set (e.g. 0x8000+).
2. DUT (UT) → DUT: SEND call.
3. Observation: DUT → Tester: data segment.

[Pass condition]
DUT emits data despite MSB-set window.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_handshake_ack — handshake never completed
• Fail_no_dut_data_segment — DUT did not send data after MSB window

verdicts.Pass: DUT honoured unsigned-16 receive window — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_dut_data_segment: DUT did not send data after MSB-set window advertisement
